80190.subject: Weekly Recap: Blast, Balancer And Abracadabra Move To Shut Down
80190.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

Three DeFi protocols put shutdown plans on paper this week, and a fourth started paying exploit victims about a penny on the dollar. **Blast** is closing its Layer 2 with about $63.5 million still in the bridge, **Balancer** holders voted to wind down and turned down an official fork, and **Abracadabra** proposed retiring MIM at roughly four cents. **Drift** opened claims on its April exploit worth about 1% of losses.

**Robinhood** switched on crypto perpetual futures for U.S. traders, up to 10x on bitcoin and ether, routed through Bitstamp and away from the **Lighter** instance in its own wallet; LIT fell 13%. **Coinbase** won CFTC approval to clear its own derivatives, and **Kalshi** filed to end its volume incentive program a week after its ether perp volume came under scrutiny.

**MetaMask** pulled its validators out of Lido after an infrastructure compromise. **NEAR Intents** lost $3.8 million and had it back within a day of naming a 48-hour deadline. Chainalysis tied the Bitget theft to North Korea, and CertiK counted $766.4 million in September losses, the worst month of 2026 in its tally.

**Base** activated Cobalt, which adds a named function for token administrators to move a holder's balance. SEC staff narrowed last week's buyback FAQ to networks with "no central party," and community banks sued the OCC over crypto trust charters.

Bitcoin ETFs took in nearly $3 billion over seven sessions, enough to turn 2026 flows positive. And the most-read story on The Defiant all week was **Coinbase** teasing Pokémon card packs.

Enjoy!

# Top Stories This Week

## Blast, Balancer And Abracadabra Moved To Shut Down

Blast said Friday it will [shut down its Ethereum Layer 2](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/blast-to-shut-down-layer-2-citing-unsustainable-costs) because "we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable." About $63.5 million remained in its canonical bridge, and users have until Oct. 26 to withdraw through the normal interface, after a roughly weeklong pause to unwind its Lido position. 🧠 Crypto News Brief: Soft US jobs data and fading Fed-hike bets lifted Bitcoin toward $87K, while regulators in Washington and Brussels advanced crypto rulebooks and institutions from Tokyo to Tether pushed deeper into on-chain finance. 📊 Weak US Jobs Report Lifts Bitcoin Toward $87K The US added just 29,000 jobs in September, far below the roughly 90,000 economists expected, while unemployment ticked up to 4.2% and August was revised down to 133,000. Bitcoin held its gains and traded just under $87,000 as markets slashed the odds of an October Fed hike to about 13%. Derivatives traders had already piled in: open interest climbed by roughly $2.3 billion since Sept. 30, and perpetual funding rates rose from about 3% to 10%. Read full story → 🏛️ SEC Proposes Crypto Custody Rules as Peirce Exits The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed a dedicated custody framework for registered investment advisers and regulated funds holding crypto. Advisers could act as custodians themselves in limited cases, such as when no permitted custodian exists for an asset, and state-chartered trust companies would qualify as custodians. Chair Paul Atkins said the plan creates a compliant pathway where none existed. A 60-day comment period opens after Federal Register publication. The proposal lands as Commissioner Hester Peirce, architect of the Crypto Task Force, departs on Friday, leaving the SEC with only two commissioners. More details → 🇸🇻 IMF Waives El Salvador's Bitcoin Breach, Releases $139M The IMF board completed the second and third reviews of El Salvador's $1.4 billion loan program and released roughly $139 million, granting a waiver even though the country breached its limit on Bitcoin accumulation. The Fund accepted documentation that the extra coins came from private donations rather than public money, but said no further accumulation is envisaged beyond documented gifts. The program also requires a smaller state role in the Chivo wallet, now majority-controlled by a private operator.
